_doc: Figure manifest. One entry per book figure: what it is, how it is made, where its facts come from and whether it has been reviewed. build.mjs builds every entry in every language; tests/figures.test.mjs checks the entries. A figure may only move from draft to reviewed once an instructor has checked it against the aircraft's own POH.
aircraft: Cessna 172N, 1979 model (factory-standard educational baseline; serial-specific configuration not verified)

figures.notes: Arc limits and the red line are POH values; the dial face layout is illustrative.

sources.what: Fuel system description: gravity feed, selector positions, strainer, primer, carburetor
Fuel quantity data: standard tanks 21.5 gal each, 43 total, 40 usable
Venting and filler caps, as cited in 08_realistic_digital_twin/data/parts_catalog.json

figures.notes: Venting arrangement (crossover line, left overboard vent with check valve, vented right cap) is Cessna's standard description for this fuel system; confirm wording and page against the aircraft's own POH during review.

sources.what: Flight controls, wing flap system and trim system descriptions (page numbers to be confirmed in review)
Planform and part names; geometry status 'estimated' except the POH span and length

figures.notes: Plan view: the planform is drawn from the POH span and the published tail span. Geometry status 'estimated'; see 08_realistic_digital_twin/docs/05_shape_reference.md.

sources.what: Engine model and rating, fixed-pitch propeller, via 08_realistic_digital_twin/data/poh_references.json
Airframe, landing gear and fuel tank descriptions (page numbers to be confirmed in review)
Shape and part names; outline fitted to photographs of the type, status 'estimated' (docs/05_shape_reference.md)

figures.notes: The grouping into five components is the usual teaching convention, not POH wording. The nose cap details (single landing light, air inlet) follow a 1970s Cessna 172; confirm against the aircraft.
